root_cause: The character class used to decide which characters are safe to leave un-escaped in the Windows cmd.exe/curl escaping function (`escapeStringWin`) used the regex shorthand `\s`, which matches a broader set of characters (tab, form feed, vertical tab, various Unicode whitespace) than just the printable ASCII space the developers intended to allow through unescaped. This over-broad allow-list let control characters that cmd.exe/CRT can interpret as token/argument separators slip through unescaped into the generated command line.
findings: The Windows cmd.exe escaping routine used by the Network Monitor's "Copy as cURL" feature (CurlUtils.escapeStringWin) builds a character class of characters that are considered 'safe' and therefore NOT escaped with the cmd.exe caret (^) escape character.
